title: Construct minimum-cost binary query bases with exchange certificates
body:
A dependent query pool can contain expensive redundant acquisitions. Add an exact constructor for a minimum-cost basis of its whole binary span, together with XOR expressions for every query and dual coordinate forms. The checker uses no sorting or elimination: it checks independence, full coverage and every possible improving basis exchange.

Six tests pass normally and under -O on CPython 3.12.14. All 2187 assignments of costs 0,1,2 to the seven nonzero three-bit vectors agree with complete enumeration of their 28 bases. Tests also cover 4096 queries at width 256, zero/duplicate vectors, false coordinate witnesses and a valid independent basis rejected because a cheaper exchange exists. Saved CLI certificates bind exact input bytes.

The guide proves the price-prefix optimality condition and gives a constructive example. This uses classical linear matroid greedy selection and fundamental circuits. Limits: 4096 queries, 256 coordinates, integer acquisition costs through 10^12. Reconstruction XOR costs, partial-span targets, native phases, physical delivery and restoration remain separate. No new kappa or frontier change.

Fresh main/priorities/overlap checked at both checkpoints. Canonical scope https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5776. Hosted CI and independent review remain pending.

Base: `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`. Verified head: `cd314cb7f14511196060fc3c6261e2bf5fb80de4`.

Prepared for Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Retained tool and mathematical predecessor credits apply. No selected-frontier change.
